1.reason: Dahil lahat ng civil servants ay public servants at si Maria ay civil servant, tiyak na siya ay public servant din.

2.question: No reptiles have fur. All snakes are reptiles. Therefore:

choices.C: All animals without fur are snakes.

2.reason: Walang reptile ang may balahibo (fur), at ang ahas ay reptile, kaya walang ahas ang may balahibo.

3.question: Some doctors are teachers. All teachers are patient. Which conclusion logically follows?
3.reason: Yung ilang doktor na teacher din ay siguradong patient dahil lahat ng teacher ay patient.

4.question: Ana is taller than Bea. Bea is taller than Carla. Dina is shorter than Carla. Who is the shortest?
4.reason: Ayos mula pinakamatangkad: Ana > Bea > Carla > Dina. Pinakamaliit si Dina.

5.reason: Modus Tollens rule: Kung nangyari ang P, mangyayari ang Q. Dahil HINDI nangyari ang Q (hindi basa ang lupa), siguradong HINDI rin nangyari ang P (hindi umulan).

6.question: All roses are flowers. Some flowers fade quickly. Therefore:

choices.D: None of the above conclusions strictly follows.

6.reason: Walang tiyak na ugnayan kung yung "some flowers" na mabilis malanta ay kasama sa grupo ng "roses".

7.question: Five runners finished a race. Mark finished ahead of Leo. Nathan finished behind Leo. Oscar finished ahead of Mark. Paul finished between Mark and Leo. Who finished second?
7.reason: Ranking (1st to 5th): Oscar (1st) > Mark (2nd) > Paul (3rd) > Leo (4th) > Nathan (5th).

8.question: All laptops are computers. Some computers are expensive. Which statement MUST be true?

choices.C: All laptops are machines, and they belong to the category of computers.

8.reason: Tanging ang premise na "All laptops are computers" lang ang 100% sigurado.

9.question: Statement: "If you pass the Civil Service Exam, you will become eligible for government service." Marco became eligible for government service. Can we conclude he passed the CSE?

choices.B: No, because there are other ways to gain eligibility (e.g., Honor Graduate Eligibility).
choices.C: Yes, because the exam is the only requirement.

9.reason: Iwasan ang Fallacy of Affirming the Consequent. Ang pagpasa sa exam ay nagbibigay ng eligibility, pero hindi ibig sabihin na iyon lang ang tanging paraan para maging eligible.

10.question: A is the father of B. B is the sister of C. C is the son of D. How is D related to A?
10.reason: Si A ang tatay nina B at C, at si D ang nanay/magulang ni C. Kaya mag-asawa sina A at D (si D ang asawa ni A).

11.question: No lazy person succeeds. Juan succeeded. Therefore:

choices.C: All hardworking people are named Juan.

11.reason: Dahil walang tamad ang nagtatagumpay at nagtagumpay si Juan, tiyak na hindi tamad si Juan.

12.question: Four friends—Alex, Ben, Cris, and Dan—sit in a row. Ben is to the immediate right of Alex. Dan is at the far right end. Cris is not next to Dan. Who sits at the far left end?
12.reason: Kung nasa dulo sa kanan si Dan (4th) at wala sa tabi niya si Cris, dapat nasa 1st (far left) si Cris. Ayos: Cris - Alex - Ben - Dan.

13.question: Every library has books. The Municipal Building has a library. Therefore:

choices.C: All books are in the Municipal Building.
choices.D: The library is closed on weekends.

13.reason: Transitive property: Municipal Building → may library → may libro.

14.question: If all squares are rectangles, and all rectangles have four right angles, then:

choices.B: All squares have four right angles.

14.reason: Ang square ay nasa loob ng kategorya ng rectangle, kaya namamana nito ang katangian ng rectangle.

15.question: Pointing to a photograph, Liza said, "He is the only son of my mother's father." Who is the man in the photograph?
15.reason: Ang tatay ng nanay ni Liza ay ang lolo niya. Ang nag-iisang anak na lalaki ng lolo niya ay kapatid na lalaki ng nanay niya—kaya tiyuhin (uncle) niya ito.

16.question: Some birds cannot fly. Penguins are birds. Therefore:

choices.C: From these two statements alone, we cannot conclude whether penguins fly or not.

16.reason: Sa formal logic, huwag gagamit ng outside knowledge; ang premise ay nagsasabi lang na some birds cannot fly, hindi sinabi kung kasama ang penguins.

17.question: Box A is heavier than Box B. Box C is lighter than Box B. Box D is heavier than Box A. Which box is the second heaviest?
17.reason: Ayos mula pinakamabigat: Box D > Box A > Box B > Box C. Pangalawa si Box A.

18.question: All honest politicians are respected. No corrupt official is honest. Therefore:

choices.C: No corrupt official is an honest politician.

18.reason: Dahil walang corrupt official ang honest, imposible silang mapabilang sa grupo ng mga honest politicians.

19.question: If today is Wednesday, what day of the week will it be 100 days from now?
19.reason: I-divide ang 100 sa 7 (araw sa isang linggo): 100 ÷ 7 = 14 weeks remainder 2 days. Wednesday + 2 days = Friday.

20.reason: Disjunctive Syllogism: Dalawa lang ang pagpipilian; dahil mali ang pangalawa, siguradong totoo ang una.

choices.B: Some fruits in the basket are sweet.

24.reason: Yung ilang engineer na musician din ay tiyak na creative.

1.question: When was the 1987 Philippine Constitution ratified?
1.reason: Na-ratify ang 1987 Constitution through a plebiscite noong February 2, 1987. It was proclaimed in force on February 11, 1987.

2.question: Where does sovereignty reside under the 1987 Constitution?
2.reason: The Constitution states that sovereignty resides in the people, and all government authority emanates from them. Ibig sabihin, ang kapangyarihan ng gobyerno ay nagmumula sa mamamayan.

3.question: What is the supreme law of the Philippines?
3.reason: The Constitution is the highest law of the land. Other laws and government actions must not conflict with it.

4.question: Which branch of government makes laws?
4.reason: Congress, composed of the Senate and House of Representatives, is responsible for making laws.

5.question: Which branch implements and enforces laws?
5.reason: The Executive Branch, headed by the President, implements and enforces laws.

6.question: Which branch interprets laws and settles legal disputes?
6.reason: The Judiciary, led by the Supreme Court, interprets laws and decides cases.

7.question: How many senators are there in the Philippine Senate?
7.reason: The Senate is composed of 24 senators elected at large by qualified voters.

8.question: What is the term of office of a senator?
8.reason: Senators serve six-year terms and may not serve more than two consecutive terms.

9.question: What is the term of office of members of the House of Representatives?
9.reason: Members of the House generally serve three-year terms and may not serve more than three consecutive terms.

10.question: What is the minimum age requirement for a Philippine President?
10.reason: A presidential candidate must be at least 40 years old on election day.

11.question: What is the term of office of the President of the Philippines?
11.reason: The President serves a six-year term and is not eligible for reelection.

12.question: Who succeeds the President if the President dies, becomes permanently disabled, is removed, or resigns?
12.reason: The Vice President succeeds to the presidency under the circumstances specified in the Constitution.

13.question: What is the minimum voting age in the Philippines?
13.reason: A Filipino citizen who is at least 18 years old and meets the other legal requirements may vote.

14.question: Which article of the Constitution contains the Bill of Rights?
14.reason: Article III protects fundamental rights and freedoms, including due process, equal protection, and freedom of expression.

15.question: What does due process mean?

choices.A: Government may punish anyone without explanation.
choices.B: A person must be treated fairly under established legal procedures.
choices.C: Only wealthy people can receive legal protection.
choices.D: Police may arrest anyone without legal grounds.

15.reason: Due process protects people from arbitrary government action. Hindi basta-basta puwedeng parusahan ang isang tao without following the law.

16.question: What does equal protection of the laws mean?

choices.B: Everyone is entitled to equal protection under the law.
choices.C: Government officials have more legal rights.
choices.D: Only citizens with jobs are protected.

16.reason: The government must treat people fairly and may not arbitrarily discriminate against similarly situated persons.

17.question: Which right protects people from unreasonable searches and seizures?

choices.C: Right against unreasonable searches and seizures

17.reason: Article III, Section 2 protects people against unreasonable searches and seizures. Warrants generally require probable cause determined personally by a judge.

18.question: What is the purpose of a writ of habeas corpus?

choices.B: To question the legality of a person's detention

18.reason: The writ allows a court to examine whether a person's detention is lawful. It is not simply a guarantee that someone will immediately be released.

19.question: Which freedom allows people to express their opinions peacefully?
19.reason: People have the right to express opinions, subject to lawful limitations and applicable rules.

20.question: What does the principle of separation of powers prevent?

choices.B: One branch from exercising all government powers

20.reason: Government powers are divided among the three branches to prevent abuse and concentration of authority.

21.question: What is the main purpose of checks and balances?

choices.B: To allow branches to limit and check one another
choices.C: To make the President more powerful

21.reason: Each branch has certain powers to prevent another branch from abusing its authority.

22.question: Which constitutional body audits government funds and expenditures?
22.reason: The COA examines, audits, and settles government accounts involving public funds and property.

23.question: Which constitutional commission administers and enforces election laws?
23.reason: The Commission on Elections is responsible for administering elections and enforcing election laws.

24.question: Which constitutional commission promotes an efficient and professional civil service?
24.reason: The Civil Service Commission oversees the government personnel system and promotes merit and fitness in public service.

25.question: Is the Commission on Human Rights one of the three Constitutional Commissions under Article IX?
25.reason: The three Constitutional Commissions are the CSC, COMELEC, and COA. The CHR is a separate independent office established under Article XIII.

26.question: Who has the power to declare martial law under the Constitution?
26.reason: The President may declare martial law or suspend the privilege of the writ of habeas corpus in cases of invasion or rebellion when public safety requires it.

27.question: What is the maximum initial period of a martial law declaration under the Constitution?
27.reason: The initial declaration cannot exceed 60 days. Congress may revoke or extend it under the conditions and procedures provided by the Constitution.

28.question: What is the main purpose of the constitutional provision on national territory?

choices.A: To establish private ownership of all islands
choices.B: To define the territory under Philippine sovereignty or jurisdiction
choices.D: To give other countries control over Philippine waters

28.reason: Article I describes the Philippine archipelago and other territories over which the Philippines has sovereignty or jurisdiction.

29.question: Which institution has the power of judicial review?
29.reason: The Supreme Court may review cases involving the constitutionality or validity of government acts, subject to the requirements of judicial review.

30.question: What is the primary purpose of the Constitution's Preamble?

choices.B: To state the ideals and purposes of the Filipino people

30.reason: The Preamble introduces the Constitution's goals and guiding principles, such as justice, freedom, equality, peace, and the common good.

1.question: What is the full title commonly associated with RA 6713?

choices.B: Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees

1.reason: RA 6713 establishes ethical standards and responsibilities for public officials and employees.

2.question: What principle does RA 6713 uphold?

choices.A: Public office is a private business.
choices.B: Public office is a public trust.
choices.C: Public office is a family inheritance.
choices.D: Public office is a personal privilege.

2.reason: Public officials are entrusted with authority and must serve the people responsibly.

3.question: Who are generally covered by RA 6713?

choices.C: Public officials and employees, whether permanent or temporary

3.reason: The law broadly covers public officials and employees in government, including government-owned or controlled corporations.

4.question: Which of the following is a norm of conduct under RA 6713?
4.reason: Public officials must prioritize public interest over personal interest.

5.question: What does professionalism mean in public service?

choices.B: Performing duties with competence and proper conduct

5.reason: Public employees should perform their duties professionally, competently, and with dedication.

6.question: What does political neutrality require?

choices.B: Providing service without unfair political discrimination

6.reason: Government services must be provided fairly regardless of a person's political beliefs or affiliations.

7.question: What does responsiveness to the public mean?

choices.B: Providing prompt, courteous, and adequate service

7.reason: Government employees should respond to public needs efficiently and respectfully.

8.question: What does simple living mean under RA 6713?

choices.B: Public employees should live within their lawful means and avoid extravagant lifestyles.
choices.C: Public employees must live in rural areas.

8.reason: Officials should avoid extravagant or ostentatious displays of wealth inconsistent with their income and position.

9.question: What does commitment to democracy require from public officials?
9.reason: Public servants must uphold democracy and respect the Constitution and democratic processes.

10.question: What is the meaning of justness and sincerity?
10.reason: Public officials should act fairly and honestly in their dealings with the public.

11.question: What is a SALN?

choices.B: Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth

11.reason: SALN is a declaration of an official's assets, liabilities, and net worth, together with required disclosures.

12.question: When must a covered public official generally file a SALN after assuming office?
12.reason: RA 6713 requires filing within 30 days after assumption of office.

13.question: When is the annual SALN generally due?

14.question: When must a covered official file a SALN after separation from service?
14.reason: The law requires filing within 30 days after separation from the service.

15.question: Which of the following should be disclosed in a SALN?
15.reason: SALN includes real and personal property, other assets, liabilities, and business interests and financial connections.

16.question: What is a conflict of interest?

choices.A: A situation where personal interests may improperly influence official duties
choices.B: A disagreement between two private citizens
choices.D: A government employee taking a vacation

16.reason: A conflict arises when private interests could affect or appear to affect impartial performance of official responsibilities.

17.question: What should a public official do when a conflict of interest exists under the applicable rules?

choices.B: Disclose and address it as required by law

17.reason: The official must comply with the disclosure and divestment requirements that apply to the particular situation.

18.question: Which act is prohibited under RA 6713?

choices.C: Having a financial or material interest in a transaction requiring approval by one's office, subject to the law

18.reason: RA 6713 prohibits certain financial and material interests in transactions requiring approval by the official's office.

19.question: Can a public official use confidential information obtained through office for personal benefit?

choices.B: Yes, if the amount is small

19.reason: Public officials must not misuse confidential or classified information acquired through their official functions.

20.question: What does RA 6713 say about accepting gifts?

choices.B: Public officials may accept any gift from anyone.
choices.C: Accepting gifts in connection with official duties may be prohibited, subject to specific legal exceptions.
choices.D: Gifts are allowed if not reported.

20.reason: The law prohibits soliciting or accepting gifts connected with official duties or transactions, while recognizing limited exceptions under its provisions.

21.question: What should a government employee do if offered money to speed up a government transaction unlawfully?

choices.B: Refuse and report the improper offer through proper channels
choices.D: Accept it if no one sees

21.reason: Bribery and improper benefits violate ethical and legal standards.

22.question: Which behavior demonstrates accountability?

choices.B: Taking responsibility for official actions and decisions

22.reason: Public officials are accountable to the people for their conduct and performance.

23.question: What is the purpose of public disclosure of SALN?
23.reason: SALN requirements help promote honesty and accountability in public service. Access is governed by applicable laws and rules.

24.question: Which of the following is an example of political neutrality?

choices.A: Refusing to process an application because the applicant supports the opposition
choices.B: Processing applications fairly regardless of political affiliation
choices.D: Using government vehicles for political campaigns

24.reason: Government employees must not discriminate based on political affiliation.

25.question: What is the main purpose of the government's Citizen's Charter under the related anti-red-tape framework?

choices.B: To inform the public about government services, requirements, fees, and processing times
choices.D: To prevent citizens from filing applications

25.reason: The Citizen's Charter helps people understand how to access government services. This is associated with anti-red-tape laws, particularly RA 11032.

26.question: Which action shows commitment to public interest?

choices.A: Giving government contracts to friends without lawful process
choices.B: Prioritizing public welfare over personal gain
choices.C: Using government property for private business
choices.D: Delaying public service for personal reasons

26.reason: Public interest must come before private or personal interests.

27.question: What is the general penalty under RA 6713 for violations of the Act?

choices.A: Only a verbal warning in all cases
choices.B: Fine, imprisonment, or both, as provided by the law

28.question: What is the main purpose of recognizing exemplary public service?

choices.B: Basic rights and freedoms belonging to every person

choices.B: Everyone is entitled to equal protection under the law.

choices.B: The right to force others to follow a religion

choices.D: The right to prevent others from worshipping

8.question: What is the right to education intended to promote?

9.question: What is the meaning of peace?

10.question: What is conflict resolution?

17.question: What is the Commission on Human Rights (CHR)?

choices.B: A decrease in all ocean temperatures
